records.claim: A UK Student visa applicant must be 16 or over and have an offer for a qualifying course from a licensed student sponsor, with a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS).
records.methodology: Direct review of current GOV.UK Student visa eligibility guidance

records.claim: For applicants who must prove funds, the Student visa maintenance requirement is £1,529 per month for up to 9 months in London or £1,171 per month for up to 9 months outside London, in addition to the required course-fee funds; exemptions and differential-evidence rules apply in specified circumstances.
records.methodology: Direct review of current GOV.UK Student visa financial guidance

records.claim: A UK Skilled Worker applicant must have a confirmed job offer from an approved UK employer, a Certificate of Sponsorship, an eligible occupation and the required English-language ability, with role-specific eligibility rules applying.
records.methodology: Direct review of current GOV.UK Skilled Worker overview and eligibility guidance

records.claim: The usual Skilled Worker salary requirement is at least £41,700 per year or the applicable going rate for the occupation, whichever is higher; specified lower-salary routes and transitional rules can apply.
records.methodology: Direct review of current GOV.UK Skilled Worker salary guidance

records.claim: Non-EEA students must meet Ireland's applicable study-permission requirements and study on an eligible programme; visa-required students have their financial capacity assessed during the visa process and students staying over 90 days must register their immigration permission.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Immigration Service Delivery student guidance and FAQ

records.claim: For a one-year course, students must demonstrate access to at least €10,000 for living costs; for stays of 8 months or less, the requirement is €833 per month or €6,665 in total, whichever is the lesser, alongside applicable course-fee evidence.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Immigration Service Delivery student-finance guidance

records.claim: Critical Skills Employment Permit eligibility depends substantially on the occupation and remuneration, and requires a qualifying job offer from a bona-fide employer in Ireland; the applicable Critical Skills Occupations List and permit rules determine whether the role qualifies.
records.sourceAuthority: Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment
records.methodology: Direct review of current DETE Critical Skills Employment Permit guidance and occupation-list framework

records.claim: From 1 March 2026, the Critical Skills Employment Permit minimum annual remuneration threshold is €40,904 for the specified qualifying occupations, with €36,848 applying to qualifying recent graduates and €68,911 applying to the higher-remuneration category; role-specific rules and the applicable occupation list still govern eligibility.
records.sourceAuthority: Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment
records.methodology: Direct review of current DETE remuneration and eligibility guidance
